# mockup-canvas

> mockup-canvas is a free, open-source (MIT) Claude Code plugin by chrisjo-dev, also usable from OpenAI Codex, made of three skills that cover plan, review, and build. mockup-canvas has your AI agent draw screen mockups as plain HTML files and lays them out on a local, Figma-like canvas where you pan, zoom, arrange, link with flow arrows, and approve them. mockup-review has an agent review those screens and leave severity-tagged findings as comments on the exact artboards. mockup-to-code turns approved screens into real code in your app and visually compares each running route with its mockup (pixel diff with side-by-side and diff images) until only intentional differences remain. It runs on the Python standard library with no pip dependencies and uses Google Chrome (or Chromium/Edge) only to render and capture PNGs.

## Key facts

- Live demo (read-only, pan and zoom only): https://chrisjo-dev.github.io/mockup-canvas/ shows the six-screen TrailMate example canvas, exported with `canvas export`.
- Three skills, one CLI: `mockup-canvas` (draw mockups and record approvals), `mockup-review` (review boards with `[must]`, `[should]`, `[could]` comments and a `review.md` report; never edits boards or sets status), `mockup-to-code` (build approved boards in the app, compare each route with its board, record the route and files). Flow: draw, review, approve, build, compare. Only boards the user approved are built.
- Install as a Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas`, then `/plugin install mockup-canvas@mockup-canvas`.
- Manual install for Claude Code and Codex: `git clone https://github.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas.git`, then `./install.sh` (links every skill into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.codex/skills`; `--claude`, `--codex`, `--dry-run` are available). `install.sh` needs a POSIX shell.
- In Codex, call the skills with `$mockup-canvas`, `$mockup-review`, or `$mockup-to-code`, for example `Use $mockup-canvas to draw the sign-up flow.`
- The CLI is one Python 3 file of about 4,600 lines (Python 3.8+, standard library only) with 18 commands: serve, roots, new, add, group, render, check, overview, export, link, status, artifact, snap, compare, impl, comment, trash, restore.
- `snap <url> --out FILE.png [--size ...] [--wait MS] [--full-page]` screenshots a running app page (http or https) at an exact size. `render --full-page` captures a board's whole scroll height. `add` with a new `--size` resizes a registered board.
- `compare <idea dir> <file> (--url URL | --png FILE)` renders the board at its registered size, captures the app at the same size, and writes `board.png`, `app.png`, `diff.png`, `side.png`, and `report.json` (with `mismatch_percent`) to `<idea>/compare/<board id>/`. A pixel differs when any channel differs by more than `--threshold` (default 24 of 255). `--ignore-top N`, `--ignore-bottom N`, and `--align-top N` handle fake status bars and home indicators drawn on boards; `--wait MS` defaults to 3000. The percentage is a guide; the images are the evidence.
- `impl <idea dir> <file> --route PATH --file PATH` records which route and files implement a board; `impl <idea dir> [--strict]` lists approved boards and whether each is implemented (`--strict` exits 1 when one is missing). `comment <idea dir> <file> TEXT [--by NAME]` adds a review comment (`--clear` removes them, no text lists them).
- The canvas shows a violet `built` badge on implemented boards and a comment count that opens a comment panel. With many boards it keeps live pages only near the view, shows cached PNG thumbnails when zoomed out (below about 30 to 40%) when served, never shows a board it has painted as a blank card again, and batches updates once per animation frame.
- `canvas serve` binds to `127.0.0.1` on port 4400 by default. `http://localhost:4400/` is a dashboard of every registered project: idea cards with board thumbnails, a status meter, comment, built, and `N new` counts, status filters (needs decision, has comments, approved but not built, built), search and a command palette (`/` or `Cmd+K`), adding, finding, renaming, and removing projects, missing folder warnings, light and dark themes, and a phone layout. `/<project>/<idea>/` is one idea's canvas, and `#<board>` fits one board. `serve <design dir>` serves one design folder at `/<idea>/`; `--port N` picks another port. In the background: `nohup python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/canvas.py serve > /tmp/mockup-canvas.log 2>&1 &`, stopped with `lsof -ti tcp:4400 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill`. The tool itself makes no outbound requests; artboards may load Google Fonts, the only external resource the skill allows.
- Share mode (`serve <design dir> --share`) is opt-in: it binds to the local network, requires a random token, is read-only unless `--share-edit` is passed, and stops after `--minutes` (1 to 240, default 30). In registry mode, `serve --share --project NAME` shares one project; a registry share is frozen to the projects registered at start and hides folder paths. Traffic is plain HTTP.
- Server hardening: requests whose `Host` header is not this server get 421 (DNS rebinding); layout saves and registry changes need a same-origin `Origin` and exactly `application/json`; artboards are served with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` and shown in sandboxed iframes; connections time out after 15 s and are capped at 64.
- `export <idea dir> <output dir>` refuses an output folder that is, is inside, or contains the idea folder, and skips symlinks pointing outside the idea folder.
- Idea folder layout: `<project>/design/<idea>/` with `canvas.json` (layout, groups, flow arrows, status and notes, impl records, comments), `boards/*.html` (one screen per file), `shared/tokens.css`, `assets/`, `render/` (generated PNGs), `compare/` (compare output), and `review.md` (the mockup-review report).
- Artboard size presets: mobile 390x844, tablet 768x1024, desktop 1440x900, or any `WxH`.
- Approvals are recorded with `canvas status <idea dir> <file> approved --note "..."`; old screens are kept in an `old drafts` group as rejected instead of being deleted. When the user asks for a delete, `canvas trash` moves an idea or a board to `design/.trash/` (the dashboard and canvas do the same, with Undo), and `canvas restore` puts it back.
- App code comes only after approval: mockup-to-code implements approved boards in the app's own framework and tokens and reports what it verified versus what it could not.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/README.md): overview, dashboard, quick start, running the server, CLI reference, security model, FAQ
- [Skill guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/docs/skill.md): every workflow step of the three skills with commands, rules, and customization
- [mockup-canvas SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/skills/mockup-canvas/SKILL.md): the instructions the agent loads to draw mockups
- [mockup-review SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/skills/mockup-review/SKILL.md): the instructions for reviewing mockups
- [mockup-to-code SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/skills/mockup-to-code/SKILL.md): the instructions for building approved mockups and comparing them with the app
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/CHANGELOG.md): changes per release
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, tests, design rules, commit style, and how to propose UI changes
- [SECURITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/SECURITY.md): threat model and vulnerability reporting

## Code

- [canvas.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/skills/mockup-canvas/scripts/canvas.py): the CLI and local canvas server
- [install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/install.sh): manual installer for Claude Code and Codex
- [plugin.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/.claude-plugin/plugin.json): Claude Code plugin manifest

## Examples

- [TrailMate example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjo-dev/mockup-canvas/main/examples/trailmate/canvas.json): a six-screen sample idea with shared tokens, flow arrows, and approval marks. From the repository root, run `python3 skills/mockup-canvas/scripts/canvas.py serve examples` and open `http://127.0.0.1:4400/trailmate/`.
